'''Arno Donda''' (28 April 1930 – 24 November 2008) was an [[East Germany|East German]] economist and statistician.  Between July 1963 and October 1990 he was in charge of the [[:de:Zentralverwaltung für Statistik|East German Statistical Authority (''"Staatliche Zentralverwaltung für Statistik"'')]].<ref name=ADlautwww>{{cite web|url=https://www.bundesstiftung-aufarbeitung.de/wer-war-wer-in-der-ddr-%2363;-1424.html?ID=608| title=Donda, Arno * 28.4.1930, † 24.11.2008 Leiter der Staatlichen Zentralverwaltung für Statistik|work= Wer war wer in der DDR?|author=[[Helmut Müller-Enbergs]]|publisher=Ch. Links Verlag, Berlin & Bundesstiftung zur Aufarbeitung der SED-Diktatur, Berlin|accessdate=5 March 2018}}</ref><ref name= "KuhrtBuck2013">{{cite book|author1=Günther Buch (compiler of "biographical notes")|author2=Eberhard Kuhrt (editor)| author3=Hannsjörg F. Buck (editor)|author4=Gunter Holzweißig (editor)|title=Biographische Notizen .... Arno Donda|work=Die wirtschaftliche und ökologische Situation der DDR in den 80er Jahren|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=GNnPBgAAQBAJ&pg=PA298|date=9 March 2013|publisher=Springer-Verlag|isbn=978-3-322-95835-8|page=298}}</ref><ref name=ADlautLeiSoz>{{cite web|work=Sitzungsberichte .... Nachrufe auf verstorbene Mitglieder| url= https://leibnizsozietaet.de/wp-content/uploads/2012/11/04_nachrufe1.pdf| author=Alfred Lachnit| pages=50–52| date=2010| publisher= Leibniz-Sozietät der Wissenschaften zu Berlin e.V.| title=Prof. Dr. habil. Dr. h.c. Arno Donda * 28.4.1930 † 24.11.2008| accessdate=5 March 2018}}</ref>

== Life ==
Arno Donda was born in Berlin.   His father worked as a typesetter. He attended middle school in [[Rumburk|Rumburg]] and [[Berlin]] before transferring, in 1947, to an apprenticeship with the main office of the statistic office in the region that was, by this time, [[Soviet Military Administration in Germany|administered as]] the [[Soviet occupation zone]].  He left the school before attempting [[Abitur|school final exams (''"Abitur"'')]], but by attending evening classes he was able to sit for and passed these exams in 1949 in Berlin as an external student, which opened the way to a university-level education.<ref name=ADlautwww/><ref name=ADlautLeiSoz/>

In 1947 he joined the [[Socialist Unity Party of Germany|Socialist Unity Party (''"Sozialistische Einheitspartei Deutschlands"'' / SED)]], a new political party formed in the Soviet zone during April 1946, through a [[Merger of the KPD and SPD into the Socialist Unity Party of Germany|contentious political merger]].   The creation of the SED was presented as a way to prevent a repeat victory of right-wing populism by ensuring that the political left was unified.   However, by the time the region was rebranded and relaunched, in October 1949, as the [[German Democratic Republic|German Democratic Republic (East Germany)]] the SED was itself coming to be recognised as the ruling party in a new kind of [[One-party state|one-party]] [[Constitution of East Germany|dictatorship]].   During 1949 Arno Donda obtained a job in the main office of the national Trade Commission, promoted to the position of "kommissarisches Leiter" by 1950, which was when he enrolled as a student at Berlin's [[:de:Hochschule für Ökonomie Berlin|Economics Academy (''"Hochschule für Ökonomie"'' / HfÖ)]].   He concluded his course in 1954 with a degree in economics.   Donda stayed on at the HfÖ, successively as an assistant, a chief assistant and a lecturer.   He received his doctorate in economics in 1957.   His dissertation concerned the relationship between retail prices and the cost of living.<ref name=ADlautwww/>   In 1959 he became Director of the Institute for Statistics at the HfÖ, retaining the position till his unexpected career switch in 1963.   He obtained his [[habilitation|habilitation (higher academic qualification)]] in 1962, becoming a professor as a result.<ref name=ADlautLeiSoz/>   This time his dissertation concerned the statistical reflection of the dynamics of performance and inputs in socialist retail trade in East Germany (''"Die statistische Widerspiegelung der Dynamik von Leistung und Aufwand im sozialistischen Einzelhandel der DDR"'').   He was also appointed a member of the [[Bernau bei Berlin|Bernau]] working group mandated to develop the so-called [[New Economic System |New Economic System of Planning and Management (''"Neues Ökonomisches System der Planung und Leitung"''/ NÖS)]].<ref name=ADlautwww/>

On 19 December 1962 [[Heinz Rauch]], his wife, and two of his three sons were killed in a [[1962 LOT Vickers Viscount Warsaw crash|plane crash in Warsaw]].   Rauch was head of the [[:de:Zentralverwaltung für Statistik|East German Statistical Authority (''"Staatliche Zentralverwaltung für Statistik"'')]] at the time.<ref name=HRlautwww>{{cite web|url=https://www.bundesstiftung-aufarbeitung.de/wer-war-wer-in-der-ddr-%2363;-1424.html?ID=2767| title=Rauch, Heinz * 23.11.1914, † 19.12.1962 Leiter der staatlichen Zentralverwaltung für Statistik|work= Wer war wer in der DDR?|author=Michael F. Scholz|publisher=Ch. Links Verlag, Berlin & Bundesstiftung zur Aufarbeitung der SED-Diktatur, Berlin|accessdate=5 March 2018}}</ref>   Despite being only 33, Arno Donda was appointed to take on the position.<ref name=ADlautLeiSoz/>   Reflecting the inherently political focus of the statistical authority, Donda took over Rauch's seat on the [[Council of Ministers of East Germany|Ministerial Council]] [[:de:Ministerrat der DDR (1963–1967)|between 1963 and 1967]].   He was also a member, between 1967 and 1990, of the [[Comecon]] standing committee for statistics.<ref name=ADlautwww/>   Between 1971 and 1990 he was a member of the [[International Statistical Institute]], based in [[Leidschenveen-Ypenburg|Leidschenveen-Ypenburg (den Haag)]]):  while a member of that he became a founder member, in 1979, of the institute's commission for constructing a "Code of Ethics for Statisticians",<ref name=ADlautwww/> which the institute subsequently accepted, by a resolution of its general assembly, on 21 August 1985.<ref name=ProfEthixlautISI>{{cite web|url=https://www.isi-web.org/index.php/news-from-isi/34-professional-ethics/296-declarationprofessionalethics-2010uk?showall=&start=4|work=The Committee was chaired by Roger Jowell. Original members were W. Edwards Deming, Arno Donda, Helmut V. Muhsam and Edmund Rapaport, who subsequently ...|title=Declaration on Professional Ethics .... Preamble .... Background Note .... Footnote 1| page=5| publisher=International Statistical Institute - Permanent Office, The Hague|accessdate=5 March 2018}}</ref>   Despite the mutual suspicions arising from the [[Cold War]] tensions of the period, Arno Donda was widely respected in the international statistics community for his ability and integrity.   Between 1980 and 1985 he served as vice-president of the Conference of European Statisticians:  in 1987 he was its president.   He also belonged to several other international  academic institutions.<ref name=ADlautLeiSoz/>   On the domestic front, he became a corresponding member of the [[German Academy of Sciences at Berlin|(East) German Academy of Sciences]] in 1979.<ref name=ADlautwww/>

== The Schürer report and the changes==
Arno Donda was a co-author of the so-called Schürer report, presented on 30 October 1989.   Other members of Schürer's team of economic experts included [[Ernst Höfner (politician)|Ernst Höfner]] and [[Alexander Schalck-Golodkowski]].   The report comprised an "Analysis of the Economic Condition of the German Democratic Republic, with conclusions" (''"Analyse der ökonomischen Lage der DDR mit Schlußfolgerungen"'').<ref name=Analyse1989>{{cite web|url=http://www.chronik-der-mauer.de/material/178898/sed-politbuerovorlage-analyse-der-oekonomischen-lage-der-ddr-mit-schlussfolgerungen-30-oktober-1989|title=SED-Politbürovorlage: Analyse der ökonomischen Lage der DDR mit Schlußfolgerungen, 30. Oktober 1989|author1=Gerhard Schürer (lead author)|author2=Gerhard Beil, Alexander Schalck, Ernst Höfner & Arno Donda (co-authors)|publisher=Zentrum für Zeithistorische Forschung e.V., Potsdam & Bundeszentrale für politische Bildung, Bonn| work=Chronik der Mauer|accessdate=6 March 2018}}</ref>   It had been commissioned by the newly appointed Party Secretary [[Egon Krenz]], for presentation to the [[Socialist Unity Party of Germany#Politburo of the Central Committee|Politburo]].<ref name=AnalyselautBStU>{{cite web|url= http://www.bstu.bund.de/DE/Wissen/DDRGeschichte/Revolutionskalender/Oktober-1989/Dokumentenseiten/30-Oktober_d/30_okt_01_text.html|title=Gerhard Schürer, Gerhard Beil, Alexander Schalck, Ernst Höfner und Arno Donda: "Vorlage für das Politbüro des ZK der SED. Analyse der ökonomischen Lage der DDR mit Schlußfolgerungen" ... Geheime Verschlusssache ZK 02 47/89 -666- Geheimhaltungsgrad darf nicht verändert werden.|date=30 October 1989| publisher=Der Bundesbeauftragte für die Unterlagen des Staatssicherheitsdienstes der ehemaligen Deutschen Demokratischen Republik (BStU), Berlin|work=Anlage Nr. 4 zum Protokoll Nr. 47 vom 31. Oktober 1989 |accessdate=9 June 2016}}</ref>   The analysis disclosed a catastrophic picture.   The East German economy was over-indebted and had for years "been consuming itself" (''"zehrt seit Jahren von der Substanz"'').   A far reaching economic reform programme was proposed, but in the view of the authors that would not be enough to avert looming national insolvency.   The only remaining hope was massive additional loans from the [[German Federal Republic|German Federal Republic (''"West Germany"'')]].<ref name=AnalyselautBStU/>

The winds of [[Glasnost]] had been blowing across from, of all places, [[Moscow Kremlin|Moscow]] since 1986 resonated strongly in the German Democratic Republic.   Street protesters breached the [[Berlin Wall]] in November 1989 and it became clear that Soviet troops had no instructions to re-enact the brutal suppression of [[Uprising of 1953 in East Germany|1953]] or [[Prague Spring|1968]].   As [[Die Wende|further changes]] unfolded during 1989/90 it turned out that the economic solution for the country would arrive not in the form of massive additional loans from the west, but as part of [[German reunification]], which was formally enacted in October 1990.   Donda successfully led the successful transition of the East German statistical authority towards integration with its formerly West German counterpart.   Till December 1991 he held the title and office, "President of the General Statistical Service of the New Federal States".   However, his task having been accomplished the Ministry officials informed him that they had no further use for his services.   It was not an unusual experience after 1990 for former senior officials of the East German state, and a sense of injustice is evident in sources.<ref name=ADlautLeiSoz/>   Between 1992 and 1994 he was registered as unemployed.   In January 1995 Donda was formally retired, reaching the age of 65 a couple of months later.<ref name=ADlautwww/>

Arno Donda died in Berlin.

Er war Mitglied der Internationalen Union für das wissenschaftliche Studium der Bevölkerung. 1979 wurde er zum korrespondierenden Mitglied der Akademie der Wissenschaften der DDR (AdW) und Mitglied des Wissenschaftlichen Rates für die wirtschaftswissenschaftliche Forschungen bei der Akademie der Wissenschaften berufen. Er war Mitglied des Gesellschaftlichen Rates der Hochschule für Ökonomie (HfÖ). Als Präsident des Gemeinsamen Statistischen Amtes der neuen Länder war er außerdem vom 3. Oktober 1990 bis zum 31. Dezember 1991 maßgeblich an der Einführung des bundesstatistischen Systems auf dem Gebiet der neuen Länder beteiligt.
